chapters.chapter: Getting started: installing OpenToonz and FFmpeg

capabilities.capability: Installers for Windows, macOS, Linux and the BSDs, with the stuffs folder (presets, brushes, profiles) set up on first run.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios image the same build onto every workstation so scenes open identically everywhere.

match.note: engine.doctor checks the container (packages, Node, Playwright, ffmpeg, models, voices) and names each fix; tools/setup.sh applies them idempotently. Doodleberry runs in one Linux container, not per-OS installers.

capabilities.capability: FFmpeg plugged in as an external encoder so the renderer can write MP4, WebM and animated GIF and import those formats.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists point OpenToonz at a system FFmpeg to get delivery codecs without extra software.

match.note: ffmpeg is a required core tool checked by engine.doctor; engine.info reports which renderers and tools are present. Encoding itself happens in film.render.

capabilities.capability: Reporting the running version and build so plugins, scripts and scenes can be matched to it.
capabilities.pro_use: Pipeline TDs pin a version for a whole production and check it before batch jobs.

match.note: engine.info lists renderers and tools; vendor.check records the version of every vendored upstream (UPSTREAM.json).

capabilities.capability: Paper pipeline: drawings scanned, registered by peg holes, cleaned, inked and painted, then composited and rendered.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios with traditional animators keep paper keys and in-betweens and digitise them in batches.

match.note: Single photos or scans become raster-part puppets in the artist's line; frame-by-frame paper sequences (registration, levels, exposure) are WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Paperless pre-production: designs and storyboard panels made in the tool before animation starts.
capabilities.pro_use: Directors lock the board before layout so every scene's assets are known up front.

match.note: Storyboards are generated from shots.json and format templates rather than drawn panel by panel.

capabilities.capability: Animatic: boards timed against reference audio with rough camera moves.
capabilities.pro_use: Editors and directors judge pacing on the animatic before committing to animation.

match.note: Storyboard stills held over the film's sound as build/animatic.mp4.

capabilities.capability: Reusable libraries of modular characters, props, backgrounds, turnarounds and motion cycles.
capabilities.pro_use: Series reuse the same rigs and cycles across many episodes to keep cost down.

match.note: Cast library with provenance; template-level clip library (walk, wave and others) retargets to every character; 16 code-drawn sets.

capabilities.capability: Layout stage: library assets placed in each scene with rough camera and timing.
capabilities.pro_use: Layout artists block scenes so animators start from correct staging.

match.note: Placement keys, sets and camera keys (or automatic coverage) are fields in shots.json.

capabilities.capability: A colour model fixed early so every character and prop keeps consistent colours through ink and paint.
capabilities.pro_use: Colour designers deliver a reference palette that painters must follow.

match.note: Puppets use named palette slots and puppet.lint flags raw colours; brand kits are measured; colour models and per-scene palette variants are WP-16.

capabilities.capability: Rooms: named workspaces, each a saved layout of panes for one task (drawing, timing, painting, rendering).
capabilities.pro_use: Artists switch rooms per task instead of rearranging windows.

match.note: Doodleberry is agent-native: the interface is the command registry (CLI, HTTP, MCP) plus fixed Studio pages (/timeline, /board, /doodle, /actout, Rig Canvas). Role-specific command subsets for agents are WP-21.

capabilities.capability: Dockable, floating and lockable panes (viewer, xsheet, timeline, schematic, function editor, palette, level strip).
capabilities.pro_use: Leads lock a room layout so the team sees the same tools in the same place.

match.note: No user-arranged window layout; Studio pages are fixed views served by dbe/server.py.

capabilities.capability: Interface themes built from editable stylesheets and a choice of interface language.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios ship a house theme and localised UI to international crews.

match.note: Single in-house owner; Studio has one theme. Film-content localisation is separate (film.localize).

capabilities.capability: A command bar of favourite commands and a searchable list of every command.
capabilities.pro_use: Power users pin the few operations they repeat all day.

match.note: engine.commands lists every command with its input schema (what agents see as tools); per-role favourites and subsets are WP-21.

capabilities.capability: History pane with step-by-step undo and redo.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists back out of a bad edit several steps without reloading.

match.note: Films are plain text, so every change is a git diff that can be reverted; a per-change audit log of who changed what is WP-39.

capabilities.capability: Record Audio pane that captures a voice or scratch track straight into the scene.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators record scratch dialogue to time a scene before the real voice arrives.

match.note: Human voice-over import with phone-level alignment and fitting into slots is in WP-13; there is no in-app recorder.

capabilities.capability: A project root shared by every machine so all artists see the same projects.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios mount one shared project root so scenes and assets resolve the same everywhere.

ref: repository layout: films/, cast/, sets/, brand/, plan/
match.note: The git repository is the project root; production sessions get git worktrees (prod.launch).

capabilities.capability: Creating a project or scene that inherits settings from an existing one.
capabilities.pro_use: Supervisors set up one template project per series and clone it for each episode.

match.note: film.create makes the folder with empty brief, facts, script, shots and score; film.from_template drafts from a format; channel brand, cast and voices are inherited (WP-32).

capabilities.capability: Standard folders per project for scans, drawings, extras, outputs, scenes and palettes.
capabilities.pro_use: Fixed folder roles let scripts and the farm find files without per-scene paths.

match.note: Each film has fixed source files and a git-ignored build/ folder; cast and sets live in cast/ and sets/.

capabilities.capability: Project browser listing projects and their scenes.
capabilities.pro_use: Coordinators jump between shows and episodes from one list.

match.note: prod.status lists every film on the production board and film.get returns one film; a full catalogue/graph view of every film folder fits WP-20.

capabilities.capability: Per-scene sub-folders driven by path variables.
capabilities.pro_use: Large shows keep each scene's renders and drawings apart automatically.

match.note: Outputs always go under the film's own build/ folder; derived films (aspect, sound-off) get their own folders.

capabilities.capability: Collect Assets: copy files loaded from outside into the project and repoint the scene, so it can be moved intact.
capabilities.pro_use: Before handing a scene to another studio, artists gather every external file into it.

match.note: Every tracked third-party file must have a manifest row and provenance is recorded; external rigs stay out of git by design, so a 'gather into a portable bundle' step would extend WP-33's vendoring.

capabilities.capability: Scene settings that start from project defaults, with the option to save a scene's settings back as the new default.
capabilities.pro_use: Supervisors tune one scene and promote its settings to the whole show.

match.note: Size and fps per film; brand kit, cast and voices inherited from the channel (WP-32).

capabilities.capability: Working units: inches, millimetres, centimetres, animation fields or pixels.
capabilities.pro_use: Paper animators lay out in fields to match their peg-bar paper.

match.note: Doodleberry works in pixels on fixed artboards (puppets in artboard units, frames 1080x1920); field units are a paper convention.

capabilities.capability: Scene frame rate, plus rendering at another rate by stretching.
capabilities.pro_use: The same scene is delivered at 24, 25 or 30 fps for cinema, PAL or NTSC.

match.note: fps is set per film (30 is the QA bar) and stepped timing gives 12s, 8s or 6s; masters at other or higher frame rates are WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Camera definition: frame size, aspect ratio, pixel resolution and DPI with locks, and saved resolution presets.
capabilities.pro_use: Layout sets the camera once per show so every scene renders to spec.

match.note: shots.json size sets the frame; film.render with aspect 16:9 or 1:1 re-stages the film natively (not a crop), with per-aspect overrides in shots.json aspects.

capabilities.capability: Viewer colour calibration through a 3D look-up table for a target colour space.
capabilities.pro_use: Colourists preview on calibrated monitors to match broadcast or cinema targets.

match.note: A LUT can be applied to the output (shots.json post.lut), but display calibration and colour management (OpenColorIO, ACES) are WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Limits on undo memory and raster memory to keep long sessions stable.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists on heavy raster scenes cap memory to avoid crashes.

match.note: Renders are headless, frame-pure and per shot; there is no long interactive editing session to tune.

capabilities.capability: Scanning through supported USB or TWAIN scanners, with an automatic sheet feeder for batches.
capabilities.pro_use: Paper departments feed whole scenes of drawings through a scanner in one pass.

match.note: No scanner hardware; drawings arrive as photos or scan files (phone-first flow, doodle.snap, puppet.from_ink).

capabilities.capability: Scan modes: black-and-white threshold, greyscale or colour lines.
capabilities.pro_use: Colour mode keeps blue/red construction or shadow lines separate for cleanup.

match.note: puppet.from_ink flattens lighting and thresholds ink to alpha, keeping texture; separating coloured line types across a sequence is WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Peg-hole registration so every scanned drawing lines up for autocentering.
capabilities.pro_use: Without registration, scanned in-betweens jitter against each other.

match.note: Only single drawings are imported today; registering frame sequences belongs with drawn levels (WP-35).

capabilities.capability: Defining which levels and frames to scan (level name, frame count, step), with unscanned frames shown as missing.
capabilities.pro_use: Scan operators work from a list that tells them which drawings are still due.

match.note: Drawing requests (drawing.requests) track missing swap drawings for rigs, not frames of drawn levels.

capabilities.capability: A crop box limiting the scanned area.
capabilities.pro_use: Operators crop to the drawing area to speed scanning.

match.note: Photos are turned upright and cropped to the ink automatically; parts are cut by polygons.

capabilities.capability: Autocentering on peg holes, rotation in 90-degree steps and mirroring.
capabilities.pro_use: Cleanup aligns every frame before lines are processed.

match.note: doodle.snap turns a photo upright; registration across a sequence is WP-35.

capabilities.capability: A cleanup camera that crops and resizes drawings to a target field and resolution.
capabilities.pro_use: All drawings land at one consistent scale and centre.

match.note: Single drawings are scaled to the artboard; sequence-wide normalisation is WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Line processing for greyscale lines: sharpness, despeckling, antialiasing (including morphological), thickness and contrast.
capabilities.pro_use: Turns pencil scans into clean, paintable lines in bulk.

match.note: Lighting flattened by dividing by a blurred copy, ink thresholded to alpha, specks removed; line-weight-preserving squash for blinks.

capabilities.capability: Colour line separation: up to several line colours detected and mapped to output styles.
capabilities.pro_use: Shadow and highlight lines drawn in coloured pencil become their own styles.

match.note: Colour styles applied across frames are in WP-35's scope.

capabilities.capability: Cleanup palette created automatically from the detected line colours.
capabilities.pro_use: Painters start from a palette that already matches the cleaned lines.

match.note: Palette slots are created on vector import (puppet.import) but not from cleaned raster lines.

capabilities.capability: Live cleanup preview, a camera test of the crop, and an opacity check that colours solid, antialiased and removed pixels.
capabilities.pro_use: Supervisors tune cleanup settings on a few frames before batching a scene.

match.note: /doodle shows suggested cuts and pivots for confirmation and puppet.coach returns an annotated image; a live cleanup-settings preview fits WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Batch cleanup of whole scenes as background tasks with priorities and dependencies.
capabilities.pro_use: Overnight cleanup of every scanned scene.

match.note: Commands run as async jobs, but sequence cleanup itself does not exist yet.

capabilities.capability: Cleanup settings saved as reusable files and linked to a level.
capabilities.pro_use: One tuned setting is reused for every scene by the same animator.

match.note: The import spec (polygons, pivots, swaps and thresholds) is a reusable JSON file.

capabilities.capability: Three drawing types: resolution-free vector levels, palette-indexed raster line levels and full-colour raster levels.
capabilities.pro_use: Teams pick vector for clean cartoon lines and raster for textured or scanned work.

match.note: Puppet parts are vector strokes, raster parts or mesh strokes; drawn levels (sequences of drawings with exposures) are a new part type in WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Brush with pressure, size range, smoothing, stabilising and snapping.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators get confident lines from a tablet without wobble.

match.note: The Rig Canvas has pressure ink (perfect-freehand) and simplification; stabiliser and textured brushes are WP-18 and WP-34.

capabilities.capability: Geometric tool for rectangles, ellipses, polygons, polylines and arcs, closing and filling shapes automatically.
capabilities.pro_use: Props and backgrounds are built quickly from clean primitives.

match.note: Sets and props are drawn in code (sets/*.js); the Rig Canvas has no shape tools.

capabilities.capability: Text tool that turns typed text into editable vector outlines.
capabilities.pro_use: Signs and lettering in the drawing itself, not as overlays.

match.note: On-screen text is live-rendered from OFL fonts in the same ink; it is not converted into editable drawing outlines.

capabilities.capability: Vector reshaping tools: cut, join, pinch, pump thickness, magnet, bend and smooth strokes.
capabilities.pro_use: Cleanup artists fix lines without redrawing them.

match.note: Polygon editing of cuts is planned in WP-18; vector deformer code (Synfig core, Inkscape) is evaluated in WP-34.

capabilities.capability: Selection with move, rotate, scale and distort, by stroke, region or matching style.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists rescale or reposition part of a drawing between frames.

match.note: Lasso and transform are listed in the feature map under WP-18 and WP-34.

capabilities.capability: Converting raster drawings to vectors (centre-line strokes or outline fills).
capabilities.pro_use: Scanned roughs become editable vector levels.

match.note: Vector tracing (VTracer, potrace) of scans is WP-18; today scans stay raster parts.

capabilities.capability: Key, breakdown and in-between drawing workflow with drawings numbered automatically from the timeline.
capabilities.pro_use: Leads draw keys, assistants fill breakdowns and in-betweens.

match.note: Keys with in-between assistance on drawn levels are WP-35 (proposals from WP-43).

capabilities.capability: Automatic in-betweens between two vector extremes with linear or eased spacing.
capabilities.pro_use: Saves assistants' time on simple moves and holds.

match.note: In-between proposals for drawn levels and morphs between views are WP-43.

capabilities.capability: Rotoscoping by drawing over imported video or image sequences.
capabilities.pro_use: Reference footage gives realistic timing for complex actions.

match.note: actout.clip turns a filmed take into motion on a rig (not traced drawings); drawing over footage needs drawn levels (WP-35).

capabilities.capability: Onion skin in relative and fixed modes, tinted for earlier and later frames, per level or whole scene.
capabilities.pro_use: Essential for judging spacing while drawing frame by frame.

match.note: The Rig Canvas shows the character's rest pose faintly behind the part being drawn; onion skins over time are WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Shift and trace: a light table showing neighbouring keys that can be offset, rotated or placed along a path.
capabilities.pro_use: In-betweeners line up arcs before tracing the middle drawing.

capabilities.capability: Viewer guides: field guide, safe areas and custom guides.
capabilities.pro_use: Layout keeps important action and text inside broadcast-safe areas.

match.note: qa.run measures every word's box against the platform-safe area per aspect; brand.assets writes safe-area overlays.

capabilities.capability: Level strip listing every drawing in a level, including unexposed ones, with insert, renumber and expose.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators manage a level's drawings apart from their timing.

capabilities.capability: Sequence operations on drawings: reverse, swing, repeat, thin out, duplicate and merge.
capabilities.pro_use: Cycles and holds are built from existing drawings without redrawing.

match.note: Clips can be reversed in speed or looped on rigs, but not drawing sequences.

capabilities.capability: Merging several columns of drawings into one flattened level, and merging painted raster levels.
capabilities.pro_use: Simplifies scenes and prepares levels for hand-off.

capabilities.capability: Level processing: brightness and contrast, colour fade, antialias, binarise, adjust levels and vector line thickness.
capabilities.pro_use: Batch fixes to whole levels, especially scans, before painting.

match.note: Thresholding and speck removal happen on import; whole-level processing across frames is WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Saving levels with optional backups and saving a copy under a new name without changing the scene.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists branch a level safely while the scene keeps its reference.

match.note: Puppets are JSON under git; cast.add records content hashes in cast/provenance.jsonl.

capabilities.capability: Exporting levels as image sequences or layered files with background, antialias and scale options.
capabilities.pro_use: Hand drawings to compositing or another tool.

match.note: Puppets export as layered SVG/ORA/PSD and model sheets as PNG; print-ready transparent stills are WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Palette per level with indexed, named styles on pages; changing a style recolours every drawing that uses it.
capabilities.pro_use: Colour changes late in production update every frame at once.

match.note: Puppet colours are palette slots named after the parts they paint; sets recolour through set_opts.

capabilities.capability: Studio palette: a shared library of production palettes, with styles linked to their source so edits propagate.
capabilities.pro_use: Character colour masters live in one place for the whole show.

match.note: Brand kits are shared and inherited by a channel's films; shared character colour models and palette variants are WP-16.

capabilities.capability: Animated palettes: style colours keyed over time.
capabilities.pro_use: Lighting changes (sunset, a blush) without repainting.

match.note: Palette variants per scene (night, sick, cold) are WP-16; keying colours over time within a shot would join it.

capabilities.capability: Style types beyond flat colour: textures, generated patterns, strokes that repeat an image, MyPaint-style raster brushes.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives painted, textured or decorative looks on top of clean lines.

match.note: Line boil, toon shading and grain exist; pencil, marker and crayon line media are WP-15 and brush engines (libmypaint, Krita) WP-34.

capabilities.capability: Bulk adjustment of many styles at once (hue, saturation, value, alpha, blend between two styles).
capabilities.pro_use: Colour stylists derive night or desaturated palettes from a day palette.

match.note: A grade on the whole picture is possible (shots.json post.grade), but palette-level derivation is WP-16.

capabilities.capability: Style naming conventions applied through a name editor.
capabilities.pro_use: Consistent names let scripts and match tools find the same style across characters.

match.note: Slots follow template names and puppet.lint flags raw colours outside the slots.

capabilities.capability: Matching a palette to a reference palette within a colour tolerance.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps imported characters consistent with the show's colour model.

match.note: brand.check measures contrast and colour-blind separation, not palette matching.

capabilities.capability: Fill tool clicking, or by rectangle, freehand or polyline area, filling areas, lines or both.
capabilities.pro_use: Ink-and-paint artists fill whole frames in a few strokes.

match.note: Rig Canvas bucket fills an ink-outlined area with a palette slot; area-select fill modes are WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Closing gaps in outlines so fills do not leak, with a check view that highlights closable gaps.
capabilities.pro_use: Avoids leaks on sketchy or scanned lines.

match.note: The bucket closes gaps up to about 10 px and refuses open outlines; a visual gap check is not there.

capabilities.capability: Painting across a range of frames, or picking colours from an onion-skinned neighbour frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Speeds painting of long sequences with the same regions.

match.note: Colour styles applied across every frame are WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Selective fill that skips painted areas, and fill depth through antialiased raster edges.
capabilities.pro_use: Repaint only unfinished regions without undoing others.

capabilities.capability: Lines that take the colour of the area they border automatically.
capabilities.pro_use: Coloured lines in the style of Japanese production without extra painting.

capabilities.capability: Painting checks: ink-only, paint-only, transparency and black-background views to find unpainted spots.
capabilities.pro_use: Final check before render to catch holes and wrong colours.

match.note: Rigs are checked for raw colours, joint gaps and missing parts; per-frame paint checks on drawn levels are WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Match lines: merging lines from one column onto another level (for tone or shadow lines).
capabilities.pro_use: Shadow lines drawn separately are joined to the paint level at the end.

capabilities.capability: Colour model viewer: a reference drawing or animation to pick styles from while painting.
capabilities.pro_use: Painters copy colours straight from the approved model.

match.note: puppet.sheet gives a model sheet; colour models as references for painting are WP-16.

capabilities.capability: Exposure sheet and layer timeline as two views of the same columns-by-frames grid.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators time on the sheet; compositors prefer the layer view.

match.note: The Studio timeline (clips, emotion and gaze keys, dialogue lanes) is clip-based; an exposure-sheet view is WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Exposing drawings into cells, and replacing a level while keeping its timing.
capabilities.pro_use: Swap a rough level for the cleaned one without retiming.

match.note: Clips are template-level, so changing a cast member's puppet keeps all its timing.

capabilities.capability: Column controls: name, fold, lock, hide from preview or render, opacity and colour filter.
capabilities.pro_use: Compositors isolate layers and tint references while working.

match.note: Per-layer opacity and colour filters belong to the compositor (WP-36); shots can be rendered selectively (film.render only).

capabilities.capability: Cell timing operations: on twos and threes, each, increase or decrease step, reverse, swing, random, roll, time stretch.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast retiming of drawings and holds without redrawing.

match.note: style.step animates on 12s, 8s or 6s; clips have speed, fades and weights; cell-level exposure tools are WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Inserting or removing frames across the whole scene with keys shifting to match.
capabilities.pro_use: Opening up or tightening a scene after an edit note.

match.note: Line-relative times reflow everything after a voice change; dragging lines and shots in Studio is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Sub-xsheets: nest columns into a reusable sub-scene, open, edit in place, collapse, explode or save separately.
capabilities.pro_use: Reusable cycles and complex sections stay manageable.

match.note: film.cuts assembles inserts from other films at edit level; nested sub-compositions inside a shot fit WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Soundtrack columns: load audio files, trim and move clips, set volume, scrub with the frame cursor.
capabilities.pro_use: Dialogue and music are timed against picture in the sheet.

match.note: Voices are synthesized and placed on lines and the score is generated from score.json; waveform lanes, trimming and importing music files are WP-40.

capabilities.capability: Automatic lip sync from audio (Rhubarb), assigning mouth drawings to phonemes in a column.
capabilities.pro_use: Gets a first pass of mouth timing in seconds.

match.note: Visemes come from word and phoneme alignment; lipsync.check cross-checks against the voice and Rhubarb.

capabilities.capability: Importing lip-sync data from Papagayo-NG or Magpie files.
capabilities.pro_use: Lip-sync specialists break down dialogue in a dedicated tool.

match.note: Importing external phoneme timings fits WP-13's recorded voice-over import with phone-level alignment.

capabilities.capability: Memos pinned to a frame and column.
capabilities.pro_use: Directors leave timing notes where the animator will see them.

match.note: Notes pinned to frames; review.fix turns them into data edits.

capabilities.capability: Save, autosave, revert and rolling backups of scenes.
capabilities.pro_use: Protects work against crashes and bad saves.

match.note: film.write validates every write; history is git.

capabilities.capability: Importing or exporting scenes between projects with their files copied to the right folders.
capabilities.pro_use: Moving scenes between productions or vendors.

match.note: A film is a self-contained folder of text files referencing cast and sets by path; prod.merge brings a film's branch back into the main tree.

capabilities.capability: Printing the exposure sheet as HTML or PDF.
capabilities.pro_use: Paper sheets go to animators and to overseas studios.

match.note: contact.pdf gives notes per shot; a printable exposure sheet is WP-35.

chapters.chapter: Creating movements (stage schematic, animating objects, 3D view)

capabilities.capability: Stage schematic: a node graph of every scene object (columns, pegbars, cameras, table) and their links.
capabilities.pro_use: TDs read and fix scene hierarchy at a glance.

match.note: timeline.get returns shots, cast and clip layers as data; a node view is WP-20.

capabilities.capability: Pegbars and multi-level parenting so children add their own motion to a parent's.
capabilities.pro_use: A character rides a vehicle or a group moves as one.

match.note: Bones parent within a puppet and props switch parents (attach keys), but a scene-level null object grouping characters and props is missing; it fits WP-11's constraints.

capabilities.capability: Several cameras per scene, each with its own size and animation, one active at a time.
capabilities.pro_use: Alternate framings of the same action for editorial choice.

match.note: Each shot has its own camera keys; the same action can be shot again as another shot or hook variant.

capabilities.capability: Camera linked to an object so it follows a character.
capabilities.pro_use: Tracking shots without hand-keying the camera.

match.note: Camera grammar follows the speaker, shakes and punches in as a pure function of time.

capabilities.capability: Hooks on drawings as attach points and pivots, up to many per level.
capabilities.pro_use: Props stay in a hand and feet stay planted in walk cycles.

match.note: Anchors and pivots come from import markers; foot pins hold feet on the ground.

capabilities.capability: Tracker tool that follows image regions across frames and outputs hooks.
capabilities.pro_use: Attach drawn elements to filmed or animated features.

match.note: Region tracking in footage is missing; it should join WP-36 (compositor), with camera-motion compensation from WP-12.

capabilities.capability: Animate tool for position, rotation, scale, shear, depth and stacking order keys, per channel or all at once.
capabilities.pro_use: Core layout and cut-out animation of whole objects.

match.note: Placement keys carry x, y, scale and flip; whole-object rotation and shear keys and animated cross-character stacking order would join WP-11 (per-pose z-order).

capabilities.capability: Motion paths: objects move along a drawn path, optionally turning to its direction, with keys snapped to path points.
capabilities.pro_use: Flying objects and smooth arcs without many keys.

match.note: Characters walk along drawn paths and turn to face their direction (place.path); props travel on ballistic arcs. Follow-path for props with keys snapped to path points is WP-11.

capabilities.capability: Keys shown on timeline cells, with easing handles, constant-speed segments and cycles.
capabilities.pro_use: Timing tweaks happen right in the sheet.

match.note: Keys use a fixed smooth ease and clips loop; per-segment easing handles and a camera-keys lane are WP-19.

capabilities.capability: 3D view with depth (Z) for multiplane and truck effects; objects scale with distance.
capabilities.pro_use: Classic multiplane depth and parallax on camera moves.

match.note: True 2D multiplane depth is WP-36 (some sets have parallax depths, and scene.js films can use a three.js renderer).

capabilities.capability: Camera animation: pan, zoom and rotate.
capabilities.pro_use: Pushes, pans and Dutch angles for staging.

match.note: Camera keys [t, [cx, cy, zoom]] are folded into the bake for every renderer; camera roll is not a field.

chapters.chapter: Editing using spreadsheet and curves (function editor)

capabilities.capability: Spreadsheet of per-frame numeric values for every animated parameter.
capabilities.pro_use: Precise numeric fixes and copy-paste of values.

match.note: Keys are readable and writable as JSON; a numeric spreadsheet view is part of Studio timeline work (WP-19).

capabilities.capability: Graph editor of curves with tangent handles, linked to the spreadsheet.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators polish spacing and overshoot visually.

match.note: Curve (graph) editor for keys is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Segment interpolation types: constant, linear, speed in/out, ease in/out by frames or percent, exponential.
capabilities.pro_use: Each move gets the spacing it needs.

match.note: Keys interpolate with a fixed smooth ease and holds (views, swaps); choosing interpolation per segment is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Expressions that compute a parameter from other objects, effects, frame number and functions (wave, random, cycle).
capabilities.pro_use: Procedural motion and linked controls without keys.

match.note: Driven keys link controls to angles, shifts, swaps and z; times reference lines; text binds to data.json. General formulas on arbitrary parameters are not supported.

capabilities.capability: Parameter values read from an external data file.
capabilities.pro_use: Drive animation from measured or simulated data.

match.note: Analysis scripts write data.json and overlays bind to it (data_from).

capabilities.capability: Similar-shape curves and editing many curves at once.
capabilities.pro_use: Keep secondary channels in step with a primary one.

capabilities.capability: Stepped values on curves (hold every n frames).
capabilities.pro_use: Match curve motion to drawings on twos.

match.note: Stepped timing per shot on 12s, 8s or 6s.

capabilities.capability: Saving and loading curves as files.
capabilities.pro_use: Reuse motion between scenes.

match.note: Clips and poses are JSON and travel with the puppet.

capabilities.capability: Building a skeleton by linking part columns and setting their pivots.
capabilities.pro_use: Riggers turn a model sheet into an animatable puppet.

match.note: Layered SVG/PSD/ORA by layer name with pivots from markers or estimated; generated humanoids; Rig Canvas saves through puppet.save.

capabilities.capability: Hook-based joints so parts stay attached even when a part is a bending animated drawing.
capabilities.pro_use: No gaps at elbows and knees during extreme poses.

match.note: Bendy limbs and mesh strokes deform at joints; puppet.coach bends each joint by 50 degrees and measures any gap.

capabilities.capability: Switching a part's drawing from within the rig (drawing substitution).
capabilities.pro_use: Hands, mouths and turned heads changed per pose.

match.note: Swap sets driven by clips or controls; drawing.requests asks for missing drawings.

capabilities.capability: Forward kinematics posing that keys automatically, with global keys for scale and shear.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast pose-to-pose cut-out animation.

match.note: Clips are placed on the timeline; poses made in the Rig Canvas travel with the puppet.

capabilities.capability: Inverse kinematics with permanent and temporary pins.
capabilities.pro_use: Plant feet or a hand on a table while the body moves.

match.note: Two-bone IK, FABRIK chains and foot pins; IK/FK blending is WP-11.

capabilities.capability: Showing only the active skeleton and resetting centres and pins.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps complex rigs readable while posing.

match.note: Viewer convenience for manual posing; agents edit data directly.

chapters.chapter: Animating with the Plastic tool (mesh deformation)

capabilities.capability: Generating a triangle mesh from a drawing with set density and margin.
capabilities.pro_use: Deform painted or complex drawings smoothly instead of cutting them into parts.

match.note: Mesh strokes with skinning come from Blender cut-out rigs; meshing an arbitrary drawing inside Doodleberry would join WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Editing the mesh: move points, swap, collapse, split or cut edges.
capabilities.pro_use: Fix bad deformation around eyes or mouths.

capabilities.capability: A vertex skeleton inside the mesh that bends it.
capabilities.pro_use: Organic bends in tails, cloth and bodies.

match.note: Bones with skinning weights and bendy limbs; SVG renderer only, others in WP-14.

capabilities.capability: Several skeletons on one mesh, switched at chosen frames.
capabilities.pro_use: Turnarounds and big shape changes on one drawing.

match.note: Multi-view rigs switch views over time; a turn control drives three-quarter offsets.

capabilities.capability: Per-vertex angle limits and no-stretch locks.
capabilities.pro_use: Prevent impossible poses.

match.note: Joint limits clamp after clips, IK, pins, chains and springs.

capabilities.capability: Painting rigid and flexible zones on the mesh.
capabilities.pro_use: Keep faces or hands rigid while limbs bend.

match.note: Weights come from the Blender source rig; painting them in the Rig Canvas would join WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Parenting other levels to skeleton vertices or hooks.
capabilities.pro_use: Props and accessories ride a deforming body.

match.note: Props and faces attach to parts.

capabilities.capability: Vertex values in the function editor and in expressions (for example mirrored shoulders).
capabilities.pro_use: Fine control and linked motion on deformation rigs.

match.note: No curve editor yet (WP-19).

capabilities.capability: Applying a mesh to a sub-xsheet so a group of layers deforms together.
capabilities.pro_use: Deform a whole assembled character as one.

match.note: Deforming a composite group is missing; it should join WP-36 (compositor), with renderer support via WP-14.

capabilities.capability: FX schematic: a node graph connecting columns and effects to output nodes, with several outputs and one active.
capabilities.pro_use: Compositors build and reuse per-scene effect trees.

match.note: Finishing is a fixed ffmpeg chain (shots.json post) plus motion effects (fx); a node compositor is WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Inserting, adding or replacing effects on links and toggling each on or off for rendering.
capabilities.pro_use: Quick A/B checks of an effect in context.

capabilities.capability: Effect settings panel with preview and keyframed parameters.
capabilities.pro_use: Effects that change over a shot, like a growing glow.

match.note: post settings are static per shot.

capabilities.capability: On-screen handles for effect positions and sizes.
capabilities.pro_use: Place a light or blur centre directly in the frame.

match.note: Parameters are data set by agents; a visual editor for the compositor is WP-36 via the WP-20 graph view.

capabilities.capability: Effect presets and macro effects combining several nodes.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios standardise looks across scenes.

match.note: Finishing presets (crisp, film, warm, cool, paper, noir) exist; user macros of nodes are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Blur, glow and light effects (including bokeh and radial or spin blur).
capabilities.pro_use: Atmosphere, magic and depth cues.

match.note: Note the generic-AI-look lint (WP-04) flags blur glows, so any glow must be deliberate.

capabilities.capability: Image adjustment and colour correction effects.
capabilities.pro_use: Grade scenes for mood and continuity.

match.note: Applied to the joined picture before captions; grain has a fixed seed.

capabilities.capability: Layer blending modes (add, multiply, screen, lighten and others).
capabilities.pro_use: Shadows, light passes and glows composited over paint.

capabilities.capability: Mattes and masks (matte in/out, erode or dilate).
capabilities.pro_use: Restrict effects or reveal elements inside shapes.

capabilities.capability: Distortion and noise effects (warp, ripple, fractal noise, random wave).
capabilities.pro_use: Heat haze, water and handmade wobble.

match.note: Deterministic line boil (turbulent displacement with cycled seeds); general distortion nodes are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Motion blur computed from the movement of a layer.
capabilities.pro_use: Smooth fast action at film frame rates.

match.note: Sub-frame motion blur on fast shots is WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Line effects for drawn levels: art contour patterns, calligraphic thickness, outlines, palette filters, external palettes.
capabilities.pro_use: Stylise lines and isolate colours for compositing.

match.note: Medium simulation for vector lines is WP-15; toon outlines and rims exist (style.toon).

capabilities.capability: Generated backgrounds, gradients and colour cards.
capabilities.pro_use: Quick backgrounds and fills behind animation.

match.note: Sixteen code-drawn sets and underlay elements.

capabilities.capability: GLSL shader effects and plug-in effects.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios add custom looks without patching the app.

match.note: In-house WebGL nodes are one of WP-36's options.

capabilities.capability: Caching effect results to speed previews.
capabilities.pro_use: Iterate on top layers without recomputing heavy effects below.

match.note: Shots are re-rendered only when their content hash changes and repeated frames are linked; the static-layer cache is WP-15 and node-level re-cook WP-20.

capabilities.capability: Particle emitter using any animated column as the particle image.
capabilities.pro_use: Leaves, sparkles or debris that move like the source drawing.

match.note: Particles (rain, sparks, snow) are WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Control images that drive spawn area, size, speed, orientation, lifetime and colour by brightness.
capabilities.pro_use: Particles shaped by a logo or emitted from a region.

capabilities.capability: Birth rate, start frame and a random seed for repeatable variety.
capabilities.pro_use: Same settings give a new but reproducible arrangement.

match.note: Any implementation must be seeded so frames stay pure functions of the frame number.

capabilities.capability: Forces: gravity, friction, wind and scattering.
capabilities.pro_use: Natural falling and drifting motion.

match.note: Props fall, bounce and roll under gravity, and multi-body scenes are baked with Rapier (physics.solve), but there is no particle system.

capabilities.capability: Change over life: spin, fade in and out, growth, trails and colour shifts.
capabilities.pro_use: Sparks that cool and smoke that disperses.

capabilities.capability: Presets for rain, snow, sparkles and smoke.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast starting points for common atmosphere.

match.note: Dust puffs and speed lines (shots.json fx) and ambient set life (steam, clouds) exist.

capabilities.capability: Previewing the rendered result in the viewer, framebar showing which frames are done.
capabilities.pro_use: Quick checks of effects and timing before a full render.

match.note: Player page with live scrubbing; web player with play, scrub and frame step.

capabilities.capability: Separate preview settings (lower resolution, sub-camera region) for faster checks.
capabilities.pro_use: Directors review fast low-res previews; final settings stay untouched.

match.note: Single shots and animatics render quickly; a draft-scale or region option with a time estimate fits WP-20.

capabilities.capability: Flipbook with snapshot comparison, RGB and alpha channels, histograms and linked playback.
capabilities.pro_use: Compare takes and check alpha and levels.

match.note: Contact sheets and stills are generated; a visual diff between two versions is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Output to image sequences and movies (PNG, TIF, TGA, MP4, WebM, GIF, MOV, APNG, sprite sheets).
capabilities.pro_use: Deliverables for editorial, web and games.

match.note: MP4 (H.264/AAC), web player and Lottie exist; WebM and ProRes with alpha, GIF and APNG are WP-23, sprite sheets WP-30.

capabilities.capability: High bit depth, floating-point and linear-light rendering with gamma control.
capabilities.pro_use: Clean gradients and correct light blending for film delivery.

capabilities.capability: Rendering with an alpha channel.
capabilities.pro_use: Hand transparent animation to compositing.

match.note: Synfig and Grease Pencil render characters with alpha internally before compositing; alpha deliverables are WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Multiple rendering: separate outputs per column or FX branch.
capabilities.pro_use: Passes for later compositing (line, paint, shadow).

match.note: OpenEXR multi-pass output (beauty, line, shadow, mattes) is WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Stereoscopic output with a camera offset.
capabilities.pro_use: 3D cinema and VR releases.

match.note: Not planned; it should join WP-37 as a delivery profile.

capabilities.capability: Frame range and step settings for partial renders.
capabilities.pro_use: Re-render only a fixed section or every nth frame for tests.

match.note: film.render takes only (a set of shots); arbitrary frame ranges would join WP-20's re-cook-only-what-changed work.

capabilities.capability: Soundtrack merged into movie output.
capabilities.pro_use: Picture and sound delivered together for review.

match.note: Voices, score and effects are mixed to -14 LUFS and muxed; stems are kept.

capabilities.capability: Batch render tasks with priorities and dependencies, saved and reloaded.
capabilities.pro_use: Render queues run overnight.

match.note: Commands run as async jobs and production sessions queue beyond max_parallel; a render queue across workers is WP-38.

capabilities.capability: Multithreaded, tiled rendering to control memory on heavy scenes.
capabilities.pro_use: Large frames render without running out of memory.

match.note: One browser per CPU on frame ranges, frame-hash dedupe of repeats.

capabilities.capability: Clapperboard (slate) frames added to renders.
capabilities.pro_use: Editorial identifies scene, take and version from the first frames.

match.note: No slate; it should join WP-37's delivery profiles (or WP-22 editor hand-off).

capabilities.capability: Render farm with a controller, render servers and the app as client sharing one farm root.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios render scenes across many machines.

match.note: Distributed render workers (OpenCue, Flamenco or in-house) are WP-38.

capabilities.capability: Splitting one render into chunks rendered on different machines.
capabilities.pro_use: Long scenes finish in a fraction of the time.

match.note: Frame-pure rendering makes chunks identical to a single-machine render, which is WP-38's done-when.

capabilities.capability: Monitoring servers (state, current task, CPUs, memory) and reading logs.
capabilities.pro_use: Render wranglers spot dead nodes and failed tasks.

match.note: The production board monitors film sessions, not render nodes.

capabilities.capability: Automatic load balancing as servers become free.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps every machine busy.

match.note: Scheduling by cost estimate is WP-38 (estimates from WP-20).

capabilities.capability: Central repository with revision history of every production file.
capabilities.pro_use: Teams recover any earlier version of a scene or level.

match.note: Films are text, so they diff, branch and bisect; renders are git-ignored and reproducible.

capabilities.capability: Get and put workflow with comments.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists check out work, change it and submit it back.

match.note: A git worktree and branch per film; prod.merge refuses changes outside the film's folder.

capabilities.capability: Edit locks on files, including locks on a frame range of a level.
capabilities.pro_use: Two artists can work on one level without overwriting each other.

match.note: Assignments and locks on films and characters are WP-39.

capabilities.capability: Seeing who holds a lock and file status against the repository.
capabilities.pro_use: Coordinators know who is working on what.

match.note: Audit log of who changed what is WP-39; prod.status shows each film session's state.

capabilities.capability: JavaScript-like scripting of scenes, levels, cells and columns.
capabilities.pro_use: TDs automate repetitive setup and fixes.

match.note: Every @command is exposed to the CLI, HTTP API, Studio and MCP with a JSON input schema.

capabilities.capability: Interactive script console inside the app.
capabilities.pro_use: Quick one-off automation without writing files.

match.note: python -m dbe <command> '<json>' and MCP tool calls play this role.

capabilities.capability: Vectorising raster images by outline or centre line from a script.
capabilities.pro_use: Batch conversion of scanned material.

match.note: Vector tracing is WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Rasterising vectors and rendering scenes or single frames from a script.
capabilities.pro_use: Automated stills and test renders.

capabilities.capability: Batch file management and format conversion.
capabilities.pro_use: Clean up and convert asset folders in bulk.

match.note: Puppets convert to and from layered files; general image and video format conversion is WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Per-user configurable shortcuts for tools, modifiers, views, playback and menu commands, including multi-key shortcuts (1.8).
capabilities.pro_use: Artists adapt the tool to habits from other software.

match.note: Agents call commands by name; Studio pages are not a full drawing application.

capabilities.capability: Playback and frame-stepping keys.
capabilities.pro_use: Rapid review of timing frame by frame.

match.note: The web player supports play, scrub and frame step.

capabilities.capability: Global transparency effect with a keyable opacity.
capabilities.pro_use: Fade a layer in or out over a shot.

match.note: Clip fades blend motion, not layer opacity; overlays pop in and out.

capabilities.capability: Local transparency driven by another layer.
capabilities.pro_use: Fade parts of a layer through a shaped mask.

capabilities.capability: Linear colour space option for blending effects.
capabilities.pro_use: Physically correct light mixing.

chapters.chapter: Command-line tools (tcomposer, tcleanup, tconverter, farm daemons)

capabilities.capability: Headless rendering of a scene file with output path, frame range, step and shrink options (tcomposer).
capabilities.pro_use: Farms and scripts render without opening the interface.

match.note: All rendering is headless; frame range and shrink options are not exposed (see the rendering chapter).

capabilities.capability: Headless batch cleanup of scans (tcleanup).
capabilities.pro_use: Overnight cleanup on servers.

match.note: Single-drawing ink cleanup only.

capabilities.capability: Format conversion between image, level and movie formats (tconverter).
capabilities.pro_use: Convert deliverables or legacy assets in bulk.

capabilities.capability: Render tasks show the exact command line they will run, so it can be rerun by hand.
capabilities.pro_use: Wranglers reproduce and debug farm failures.

match.note: Every command has a JSON input schema and the same call works from CLI, HTTP and MCP.

capabilities.capability: Driving OpenToonz itself from Doodleberry data (a scene rendered by tcomposer).
capabilities.pro_use: Reuse OpenToonz's renderer and level model inside an automated pipeline.

match.note: WP-34's done-when names exactly this; WP-35 builds drawn levels on OpenToonz's level and X-sheet model if chosen.

chapters.chapter: What's new: release notes 1.6 to 1.8 (and Tahoma2D fork notes)

capabilities.capability: Preproduction board panel for laying out story panels (1.7; Tahoma2D refactored its own board in 1.6).
capabilities.pro_use: Boards and timing live in the same tool as animation.

capabilities.capability: Interchange of layered cel animation through the Open Cel Animation format (export 1.7, import 1.8).
capabilities.pro_use: Move drawn animation between Krita, Blender and other cel tools.

match.note: Rig exports exist (layered files, Synfig, Lottie); OCA in and out would join WP-22's hand-off formats.

capabilities.capability: Exposure-sheet interchange: XDTS integration (1.8), plus sheet export to PDF and TVPaint JSON (1.6).
capabilities.pro_use: Timing sheets exchanged with Japanese studios and other paint tools.

match.note: Belongs with the exposure sheet in WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Camera track export (1.7).
capabilities.pro_use: Camera moves reused in a compositing or 3D tool.

match.note: Camera keys are data but are not exported; it should join WP-22 (editor hand-off).

capabilities.capability: Navigation tags and coloured cell marks on the timeline (1.6, 1.7).
capabilities.pro_use: Jump to story points in long scenes.

match.note: Lines are named anchors that shots and clips reference; review notes are pinned to frames.

capabilities.capability: Screentone fills (1.8).
capabilities.pro_use: Manga-style tone shading.

match.note: Joins WP-15's medium and style passes.

capabilities.capability: Stroke replication (symmetry-style drawing) and improved perspective/assistant guides (1.8).
capabilities.pro_use: Symmetrical props and correct perspective in backgrounds.

capabilities.capability: New effects: Flow effect series and Floor Bump (1.7), Smoother and lazy-brush style effects (1.8).
capabilities.pro_use: Painterly flow-driven distortion and line smoothing.

capabilities.capability: OpenEXR image support (1.6) and floating-point linear rendering (1.7).
capabilities.pro_use: Film-grade intermediates.

capabilities.capability: Multithreaded FFmpeg encoding (1.6) and faster MP4 renders with audio (1.7).
capabilities.pro_use: Shorter turnaround for review movies.

match.note: Parallel capture plus -tune animation encoding.

capabilities.capability: Pasting images from the system clipboard, custom panels and a see-through main window (1.7, 1.8).
capabilities.pro_use: Interactive conveniences for artists.

match.note: Desktop UI conveniences; Doodleberry is driven by commands.

capabilities.capability: Camera capture for stop motion and pencil tests, with camera calibration (1.6); Tahoma2D adds DSLR support through Canon SDK and gphoto.
capabilities.pro_use: Capture paper pencil tests or puppets frame by frame.

match.note: actout.clip uses a webcam for performance capture, not frame capture; stop-motion capture should join WP-35 (drawn levels as image sequences).

capabilities.capability: Tahoma2D: clipping masks in the timeline and per-column alpha lock (1.6).
capabilities.pro_use: Paint inside a character's shape without spilling.

match.note: Masks and mattes are WP-36.
